title: paged-kv-cache-block-manager-reuse-and-pinning-optimizations
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: the paged KV cache block manager has been a frequent source of tail-latency and memory churn in large-chat workloads. We observed allocator churn and suboptimal eviction/pinning behavior under high concurrency and mixed sequence-length workloads. This PR improves allocator reuse, makes pinning semantics explicit and cheaper, and adds metrics and canary rollout controls. High-level changes: 1) Reuse block allocator instances across short-lived allocations to reduce allocation overhead and fragmentation, introducing a small freelist per-NUMA/socket to avoid cross-thread contention. 2) Add a lightweight pin_count on blocks with a fast-path for pinned reads to skip eviction checks and avoid needless lock acquisitions. 3) Introduce soft_ttl and a relaxed background eviction loop that respects pin state and batch-aware heuristics to avoid evicting blocks needed by in-flight streams. 4) Add instrumentation (histograms and counters) for allocator hits/misses, pin hold times, eviction skipped due to pinned blocks, and per-batch cache pressure signals used by the scheduler. 5) Expose a feature flag and rollout config to enable allocator reuse and pinning heuristics incrementally (canary -> steady -> full), with a fallback toggle for immediate rollback. Results: microbenchmarks (bench/kv_cache_microbench) show 6-12% improvement in p99 token latency for multi-stream workloads and a 9% reduction in GPU-side memory pressure due to lower temporary allocations. Integration tests show no regressions on correctness; additional stress tests added to reproduce previously-observed eviction races. Rollout: enabled behind feature flag teleport.paged_kv_allocator_reuse; staged canary on Dedicated pools for 48h before global rollout. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for allocator reuse and pin/unpin semantics - [x] Stress test reproducer and fix for prior race - [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboard updates - [x] Docs updated with new knobs and safe rollout instructions - [x] Feature flag + rollout config added
commits: paged_kv: reuse allocator instances and add per-socket freelist
block_manager: add pin_count with fast-path for pinned reads
ttl: introduce soft_ttl and relaxed eviction loop
metrics: add allocator_hit/miss and pin_hold_time histograms
scheduler: expose cache pressure hint for batching decisions
tests: add stress reproducer for eviction race
discussion: Marcus Rivera: Nice work. Can you quantify allocator reuse overhead reduction and potential contention on the freelist? Please add a microbench measuring freelist hit-rate.
Aisha Patel: Added bench/kv_cache_microbench and a new allocator_hit/miss metric. Benchmarks attached in PR description; freelist hit-rate observed ~78% under our multi-stream workload.
Elena Kovalev: Concerned about pin lifetime causing memory to be held longer than necessary. Do we have safeguards to avoid long-lived pins from a buggy consumer?

Aisha Patel: Added diagnostics and a pin_hold_time histogram, and introduced a soft_ttl that the eviction loop will consider once pins exceed a safety window. Also added max_pin_duration config with default conservative value.
Devon Brooks: CI flake on tests/kv_cache/allocator_unit_tests in the first run, looks like a timing-dependent assertion. Reran CI after adding a 10ms backoff in the test harness.
CI: Initial run failed (tests/kv_cache/allocator_unit_tests), rerun passed and all checks are green.
release_notes: Paged KV cache: allocator reuse and pinning optimizations. Reduces p99 token latency by ~6-12% on multi-stream workloads, lowers memory pressure, adds observability and a feature-flagged rollout. Backwards-compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
summary: Improve paged KV cache block manager by reusing allocators, adding lightweight pinning with fast-paths, and tuning eviction behavior. Includes metrics, tests, and a feature-flagged rollout.
